verdict.rationale: Modal ships an official Python SDK with versioned reference docs and release notes for `Sandbox`, `SandboxSnapshot` and `Probe`. Official JS and Go SDKs live in the modal-labs GitHub org and have a dedicated guide with code that creates Sandboxes, mounts Volumes and runs `exec`. Missing for 10: the JS/Go SDKs cover only "some" Modal platform resources (not full Python parity), and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of building with the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: The JS and Go SDKs allow you to use Modal Sandboxes, invoke deployed Modal Functions, and interact with some Modal platform resources.
Using Sandboxes in JS/Go projects, to safely execute arbitrary commands, run untrusted user code, or as a safe environment for AI agents.
A `Sandbox` object lets you interact with a running sandbox. This API is similar to Python's asyncio.subprocess.Process
We've added a modal.Sandbox.logs API, allowing you to fetch() logs from a specific date/time range or to tail() the most recent logs.
